title: Dodge & Burn in Photoshop - Day 19 (Non-destructive workflow with adjustment layers, masking, and Blend If)
summary: This PHLEARN tutorial (Day 19 of 30 Days of Photoshop) surveys both traditional and non-destructive approaches to dodging and burning. It begins by acknowledging the destructive nature of the native Dodge and Burn tools on the background layer, then presents a non-destructive alternative using adjustment layers (notably Brightness/Contrast) with masks that can be toggled, masked, and re-tuned over time. The instructor introduces refining these adjustments with layer masks, inverting masks, and painting with white on the mask; then shows how to isolate edits to the subject using Select Subject and grouping. A highlight is the Blend If technique, which confines dodging/burning to highlights or shadows based on the underlying pixels, enabling very natural results. The video emphasizes a non-destructive, adjustable workflow where edits remain reversible, grouped, and adjustable in real time, and it ends with a downloadable PSD/sample image for hands-on practice.
topics: Mask visibility and containment within a group
Dodge/Burn in a group with subject mask
Separating Blend If sliders with Alt/Option

sections.title: Dodge & Burn Tools: Concepts and Drawbacks
sections.description: Introduction to the dodge and burn tools, their basic effect (brighten/darken), and the key drawback: edits are baked into the pixels of the background layer, making later adjustments difficult.

sections.title: Non-destructive Dodging/Burning with Adjustment Layers
sections.description: Switch to a non-destructive approach by using a brightness/contrast adjustment layer instead of painting directly on the background, enabling on/off toggling and later recalibration.

sections.title: Mask Inversion and Revealing with Brush on Adjustment Layer
sections.description: Invert the adjustment-layer mask and paint with white to selectively reveal the brightness/contrast changes, with brush flow set for gradual buildup and precise control.

sections.title: Targeting Edits to the Subject with Select Subject and Grouping
sections.description: Demonstrates selecting the subject from the background, grouping the adjustment layers, and masking so dodging/burning applies only where the subject is visible.

sections.title: Blend If: Refining with Underlying-Layer Lighting
sections.description: Introduces Blend If to confine adjustments to image highlights or shadows, using Alt/Option to split sliders and left/right directions to selectively reveal edits for a more natural look.

sections.title: Non-destructive Summary and Practice Resources
sections.description: Wrap-up emphasizing the advantages of non-destructive dodging/burning through adjustment layers and groups, plus a note about accessing a downloadable PSD/sample image for practice.
